question_dict.question: What is the IP address associated with the Manatee Tempest activity group detected in this security incident?
solution: The account with SID `S-1-5-21-1840191660-8534830288-125585561-1522` was involved in a Command and Control behavior that was blocked.
The cybercriminal group known as Manatee Tempest, which is associated with the IP address `198.43.121.209`, was active during the incident.

You are a security analyst. 
You need to answer a given security question by querying the database.
The logs are stored in a MySQL database, you can use SQL queries to retrieve entries as needed.
Note there are more than 20 tables in the database, so you may need to explore the schema or check example entries to understand the database structure.

Your response should always be a thought-action pair:
Thought: <your reasoning>
Action: <your action>

In Thought, you can analyse and reason about the current situation, 
Action can be one of the following: 
(1) execute[<your sql query>], which executes the SQL query. For example, execute[DESCRIBE table_name].
(2) submit[<your answer>], which is the final answer to the question

You should only give one thought-action per response. The action from your response will be executed and the result will be shown to you.
Follow the format "Thought: ....
Action: ...." exactly.
Do not include any other information in your response. Wait for the response from one action before giving the next thought-action pair. DO NOT make assumptions about the data that are not observed in the logs.

On July 4, 2024, a security incident involving malware behavior named 'GenRansom' was detected on host `vnevado-win11t`. This malware was identified as active on the machine, and immediate precautionary measures were recommended. This incident is part of a broader malicious activity linked to the Manatee Tempest activity group. Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group known for engaging in various sophisticated cyberattacks targeting numerous industries. What is the URL associated with the Manatee Tempest activity group in this incident?

The logs are stored in a MySQL database, you can use SQL queries to retrieve entries as needed.
Note there are more than 20 tables in the database, so you may need to explore the schema or check example entries to understand the database structure.

Your response should always be a thought-action pair:

In Thought, you can analyse and reason about the current situation, 
Action can be one of the following: 
(1) execute[<your sql query>], which executes the SQL query. For example, execute[DESCRIBE table_name].
(2) submit[<your answer>], which is the final answer to the question

You should only give one thought-action per response. The action from your response will be executed and the result will be shown to you.
Follow the format "Thought: ....
Action: ...." exactly.
Do not include any other information in your response. Wait for the response from one action before giving the next thought-action pair. DO NOT make assumptions about the data that are not observed in the logs.

('2024-06-20 09:19:23.719343+00:00', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

For more information, read the Actor Profile: Manatee Tempest Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/a22c3410-db8f-4c58-866e-ebb760e509d0/analystreport', ('2024-06-20 09:40:00.779383+00:00', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

For more information, read the Actor Profile: Manatee Tempest Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/a22c3410-db8f-4c58-866e-ebb760e509d0/analystreport', has been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

('2024-06-20 09:19:23.690415+00:00', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

('2024-06-20 09:40:00.275880+00:00', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

For more information, read the Actor Profile: Manatee Tempest Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/a22c3410-db8f-4c58-866e-ebb760e509d0/analystreport', ('2024-06-20 09:40:00.756601+00:00', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

For more information, read the Actor Profile: Manatee Tempest Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/a22c3410-db8f-4c58-866e-ebb760e509d0/analystreport', question_dict.context: A recent security incident was flagged due to the execution of a known credential theft tool, which was used to dump user's credentials. This was detected on an account from a specific IP address.
question_dict.question: A related alert indicates the presence of a file associated with Mimikatz. Can you identify the name of this file that was detected?
solution: A known credential theft tool execution command line was detected on the host with AadDeviceId `4d8d23e9-a77d-4e33-9435-b8c457e57ca1`.
The Mimikatz credential theft tool, particularly the file `mimilib.dll`, was detected on this device.

question_dict.question: What is the command line of the process that was executed when the 'CommandAndControl' malware was detected during lateral movement?
solution: The ransomware payload was remotely launched on the account `dp5hn` at `2024-07-04 22:35:01.951341+00:00`.

The 'CommandAndControl' malware was detected during lateral movement. The attacker's command line was `curl http://vectorsandarrows.com` and it was executed with Process ID `5572` on `2024-06-20t09:32:04.8002759z`.

question_dict.context: A security incident involving the Manatee Tempest activity group was flagged, where the actor Manatee Tempest, known for its early malware campaigns like the Dridex banking trojan, has been active since June 2014. The group utilizes tactics such as drive-by downloads and FakeUpdates infections, facilitated by Mustard Tempest to gain initial access. Later, they use the BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. One of the events related to this incident involved a process running on the host `vnevado-win11t` using the command `curl http://vectorsandarrows.com`. The Process ID was 88.

FROM SecurityAlert

A recent incident associated with this group involved a suspicious HTTP request to `vectorsandarrows.com` from the IP address `198.43.121.209` using the command line: `curl http://vectorsandarrows.com`, with process ID 6460. (2) submit[<your answer>], which is the final answer to the question

Do not include any other information in your response. Wait for the response from one action before giving the next thought-action pair. DO NOT make assumptions about the data that are not observed in the logs.

('2024-06-20 09:44:54.063942+00:00', 'System recovery setting tampering', 'System recovery setting tampering', 'System recovery setting tampering has been observed on this device. Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]

('2024-06-20 09:40:00.779383+00:00', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

('2024-06-20 09:40:00.407711+00:00', 'System recovery setting tampering', 'System recovery setting tampering', 'System recovery setting tampering has been observed on this device. Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]

('2024-06-20 09:19:23.719343+00:00', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]

question_dict.context: A Mimikatz credential theft tool was detected on a device. Mimikatz is a credential theft tool that can harvest plaintext passwords, password hashes, smartcard PINs, and Kerberos tickets. Attackers may use this tool to harvest credentials to log into this or other devices on the network by impersonating a valid user. The detection of Mimikatz is part of a broader security investigation. Additionally, there was later evidence of lateral movement to the jump server `Vnevado-jump` using PSExec.
question_dict.question: A related alert indicated a possible compromised user account dropping ransomware-related files. Can you identify the name of the specific file associated with the ransomware activity?

A compromised user account was observed dropping a ransomware-related file named `get-userprttoken.ps1` on several devices.

question_dict.context: A security incident involving a possible attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT) was detected. The file `browsercore.exe` was launched with the command line `browsercore.exe` on process ID 1640 at 2024-06-20T09:32:12.1031042Z. The PRT is a key artifact of Azure AD authentication used to enable single sign-on (SSO) across devices. Attackers might attempt to access this token to move laterally within the organization or perform credential theft. For more information, check the Midnight Blizzard credential attacks Threat Analytics report.

You should only give one thought-action per response. The action from your response will be executed and the result will be shown to you.

A serious security incident involving the Mimikatz credential theft tool was detected on a device. Mimikatz is known for harvesting plaintext passwords, password hashes, smartcard PINs, and Kerberos tickets. An attacker might use this tool to obtain credentials to log into this or other devices on the network by impersonating a valid user. The tool was executed with several different command lines indicating privilege escalation and credential theft attempts. What was the command line of the process detected with the known credential theft tool execution?

question_dict.context: A security incident related to the Manatee Tempest activity group has been detected. This actor, tracked by Microsoft and known to be a Russia-based cybercriminal group, has been active since June 2014 and is notorious for its Dridex banking trojan campaigns. The group partners with Mustard Tempest to facilitate access to target networks via methods such as drive-by downloads, malvertising, and FakeUpdates infections. They use a BLISTER loader to deploy Cobalt Strike beacons for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. Recently, on host identified by `vnevado-win10s` with the AadDeviceId `f5b847aa-8712-4bf6-b4f7-ed6cd89e1505`, a process with ProcessId `6460` was initiated to execute a command to curl a suspicious URL (`http://vectorsandarrows.com`).

question_dict.context: A security incident involving the deletion of all file snapshots and shadow copies via WMI or VSSAdmin, which is common during ransomware infection, was detected. The process `vssblatemp.exe` with process ID 1900 was used to perform the deletion. This incident might be part of a larger malicious campaign as described in the Activity Profile: Iranian MOIS operators opportunistically deploy limited-impact wiper in response to Israel-Hamas war.
question_dict.question: Following this alert, we also detected malicious command and control behavior. Can you provide the URL associated with this command and control behavior?
solution: File backups were deleted on host `vnevado-win11u`, commonly associated with ransomware infection.
A command and control behavior originating from the URL `http://vectorsandarrows.com/` was blocked, indicating an active malware infection.

Adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating system data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.

Operating systems may contain features that can help fix corrupted systems, such as a backup catalog, volume shadow copies, and automatic repair features. Adversaries may stop or delete system recovery features to augment the effects of Data Destruction and Data Encrypted for Impact.

Many native Windows utilities have been used by adversaries to disable or delete system recovery features:
•	 vssblatemp.exe can be used to delete all volume shadow copies on a system using the following command: [vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all /quiet]
•	Windows Management Instrumentation can be used to delete volume shadow copies using the following command: [wmic shadowcopy delete]
•	wbblatemp.exe can be used to delete the Windows Backup Catalog using the following command: [wbblatemp.exe delete catalog -quiet]

question_dict.context: As part of a Ransomware infection observed in our organization, file backups were deleted via WMI or VSSAdmin on the host `vnevado-win10r`. The process involved was identified with ProcessId__CreatedTimeUtc__CommandLine `7236__2024-06-20t09:10:51.2193152z__vssblatemp.exe delete shadows /all`. Further investigation identified that system recovery setting tampering was observed on the same host, where adversaries might be attempting to delete or remove built-in operating systems data and turn off recovery services to prevent recovering a corrupted system. This may deny access to available backups and recovery options.
question_dict.question: During the system recovery setting tampering, what process and command line was used to disable automatic Windows recovery features?
question_dict.answer: Process Id: 4828, Command Line: `bcdedit /set recoveryenabled no`
solution: An attack was detected where file backups were deleted via `vssblatemp.exe`.

System recovery settings were tampered with using the process `bcdedit.exe` which was launched with the command line `bcdedit /set recoveryenabled no` at `2024-06-20t09:31:59.6743318z` with Process ID `4828`.

('Manatee Tempest activity group', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

('Manatee Tempest activity group', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

For more information, read the Actor Profile: Manatee Tempest Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/a22c3410-db8f-4c58-866e-ebb760e509d0/analystreport', Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

('2024-06-20 09:40:00.275880+00:00', 'Manatee Tempest activity group', 'The actor that Microsoft tracks as Manatee Tempest is a Russia-based cybercriminal group that has been active since June 2014. It was notorious for one of its earliest malware lexpaigns – the Dridex banking trojan. Manatee Tempest is also one of the first groups to be sanctioned by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) in 2019.

Manatee Tempest’s tactics rely on a partnership with Mustard Tempest, an access broker that facilitates access to target networks. Manatee Tempest has been observed targeting organizations across a diverse array of industries with methods such as drive-by download, including malvertising and FakeUpdates (also known as SocGholish) infections facilitated by Mustard Tempest to obtain initial access, followed by BLISTER loader to deliver Cobalt Strike beacons which are used for lateral movement and ransomware deployment. The actor also uses domain fronting to establish command-and-control channel for Cobalt Strike beacons. Manatee Tempest overlaps with activity tracked by the cyber intelligence industry as EvilCorp, UNC2165, and Indrik Spider.

For more information, read the Actor Profile: Manatee Tempest Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/a22c3410-db8f-4c58-866e-ebb760e509d0/analystreport', It is a JSON Web Token (JWT) that's specially issued to Microsoft first party token brokers to enable single sign-on (SSO) across the applications used on those devices. Attackers can attempt to access this resource to move laterally into organization or perform credential theft.
